That one question was whether what was contained in this document concerning Mr. Benabou and the way he was described by Mr. Sorensen was accurate and correct. And you, in fact, indicated that that was in fact true, and that will be on page 111 of your testimony today.

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: Yes, sir, your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I just want to make sure you -- you have it there?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, obviously, you've seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you were a participant in those events?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You were there live as the situation was unfolding?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you were able to see here and sort of synthesize exactly what was happening, especially the way Mr. Benabou was thinking, speaking, reacting?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: I was a witness to some of it, to some of the cases -- some of his -- him and Mr. Sorensen's confrontations. I didn't happen to be present when they were happening, but I did see that there was quite a bit of tension between the two of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you weren't present at all or were you present --

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: Sometimes. At some of the meetings, I was there and witnessed what was going on, and there were other times when there were conversations that I didn't actually see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Now, I don't want to go into too much of the specifics as to who did what or who said what and what have you. First of all, Mr. Benabou, what exactly was his position, you know? We know that he was with civilian affairs. You were with civilian police?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He was with civilian affairs, and help me out here. Is he above, is he below, is he parallel? Where is he in the --

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: In the structure?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- in the structure?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: I would think that he's probably equal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So now we're speculating?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: Yeah. He may have been considered above the UN, but I didn't -- I didn't consider him a superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. You didn't consider him a superior, because you were -- you just looked at your superior as your superior, and that was it; right?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So, in other words, Mr. Benabou didn't have any authority to order you; and if he did --

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- it was de facto wasn't recognising it?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And nobody told you he had that authority?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: No. I did find quite a bit about Mr. Benabou many -- quite a long time later, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. That's what I want to get to. Because from reading here, from what I read here, I see Mr. Benabou as being somebody who is out of control, angry, doesn't know how to negotiate, for sure, can't be trusted, indivisive, and perhaps lacks judgement?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So help us out here, because this is a report generated by your supervisor, and you said that you were an observer of some of these events. Well, help us out with this Mr. Benabou.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. Before you answer, Mr. Flynn, how many minutes do you need should you have additional redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: I think five minutes should do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So we will be able to conclude. Mr. Forbes, please respond.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was my feeling, again, my feeling --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, you were observing?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: Yeah. So, if I can offer my opinion. I'm not sure if it's permissible in the court, but my --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Hold on here. Hold on here. You were offering opinions all day long, and I didn't hear you equivocating when it came to the Prosecution saying, "Gee, Judges, don't accept my opinion." So, now, I've got a live police officer who is retired, albeit; lots of years on the street; knows people; knows how to read people, right; testified many times in court. Is that a yes to all my questions?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. There you go. So give it to us.

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Give us your opinion.

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: I felt that it wasn't completely out of control. I felt that he had an agenda and that he was acting the way he was for a certain reason, and I believed at that time that possibly he was trying to hinder the Muslim cause; and that years later, when I was guarding the Israeli ambassador to Canada, it turned out I found out that Mr. Benabou worked for, as he described it, "The Institute," or Mossad, and that he was still in their employ when us guarding the Israeli ambassador at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The Mossad?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: Yes. I must say, too, that Mr. Benabou -- and I later on when I had occasion to explain that, you know, what I found the roundup of all those civilians with the searchlights and loudspeakers was very similar to Warsaw Ghetto in 1944. And I think Mr. Benabou actually started to come around and agree with me, to a certain extent, that I saw good and bad people on all the sides, and you had to keep an open mind. And I think it was my own feeling that he had an agenda.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's step take it step-by-step. First, you indicated that you learned later on that he was Mossad?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: That was indicated to me by the Israeli ambassador to Canada.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's not in the transcript, but I assume it will get in the transcript at some point. Now, just for the transcript, let's make sure, what is Mossad? I mean, I think I know what it is, but some of us may not know. What is it?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: It's the Israeli Secret Service that operate outside of Israel gathering intelligence. They also have been known to do offensive operations to discredit who they consider to be their enemies and, you know, they've done a lot of different things outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, it says here, at some point, he had to be told, basically, to step aside because he was hindering the negotiating process?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And he was yelling at people?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: That's right. He was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He was yelling at those like the -- well, I guess the people that he would have to negotiate with, the Muslims, right?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: Right. He was upsetting them so much that actually one of the reporters from the Washington Post came to us and said, "You've got to get him out of here. He's just going to cause lots and lots more trouble."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And then, at some point, you indicated that he sort of disappeared. He and Thornberry found, I believe, accommodations for themselves and were --

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- nowhere to be found --

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: Yes, and we didn't --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- in the middle of this crisis?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: We didn't know where they were and we were trying to get hold of them, because we were negotiating to get an ambulance with four critically ill children out of there to better medical facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And, now, did you ever have a conversation with Mr. Benabou afterwards, to get him to explain why he was behaving in this erratic manner?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: No. But, as I say, later on, I had more dealings with civilian affairs later and got to know Mr. Edward Joseph quite well. And he actually sent a letter of commendation to our commissioner in Zagreb about my service; and, after a while, I think he may have said to Mr. Benabou that you know I've been in there a lot and I've seen first-hand a lot of things that he wasn't actually seeing. And I think toward the end he was starting to come around, but his shenanigans, to me, some of it would seem to be a put-on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: A put-on in the sense that he was make believing his -- it was acting?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: Yes. A good example: On the 21st of August, when we went in there, we brought the ambulance APC that had the medical supplies. We got it to the hospital, behind the hospital, and there was a lot of press there from different networks, such as, CNN and whatnot. And Mr. Benabou went right up to the front of the line. We'd sort of formed a line to pass boxes on from one hand to another to speed up the unloading and taking it into the hospital. Mr. Benabou got right into the front where the cameras were; and as soon as the cameras turned away, he just -- he walked away from and didn't continue helping any more with the unloading.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So that was just to pretend that he was doing something?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: Yeah. Show, to be seen on TV and in the international press.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it if he was behaving that way, did -- did he behave in that fashion with others as well, with other internationals or with the nationals?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: There was a number of people that were really, really upset from a number of different countries that had been witnessing this, and he just didn't seem to want to listen to anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Came with his own agenda, but also with his ideas of who the people were and who he was dealing with?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: Right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Come to conclusions?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: I think maybe, in the end, he changed his mind a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. I just have one last question, I guess, and it's -- I'm dealing -- I'm looking at one of the documents. It's a Prosecution document, and we don't have to dwell on it, but it just caught my fancy. It's 5625. On page 4, you were asked to give a description or make an assessment, I should say, make an assessment of your impressions of certain individuals. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: Yes. I wasn't actually asked to do it. I did it on my own, because I thought it might help if they understood the people; and if my assessment was correct of them, it might -- it might help the powers to be in the United Nations to see what --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: -- could happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Fair enough. If it might be correct - and I'm glad you qualified that - it looks from the first page that this is dated 20 September, or maybe I'm wrong -- I'm sorry, that's the wrong date. 6 October.

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I notice, in your assessment, to your credit or whoever put this in --

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- that it stressed that the above intelligence on the character of these people is unconfirmed, and based of limited personal contact with the writer.

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So, in other words, this is -- this is sort of a caveat. This is my impression, but I may be wrong?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it one of the reasons you indicated that you may be wrong is because you didn't know the culture?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Didn't speak the language?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: Right. Hadn't know them all that long.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Hadn't known them that long, and you certainly didn't want to jump to any conclusions on what they were thinking?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Or how they were behaving?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Or how honest they were with you?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So it would be fair to say that at least what you were observing from Mr. Benabou, we could almost say the exact opposite, at least at that point in time, when you were seeing him, working with him, and dealing with him back in August 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, thank you very much. Have a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution for redirect.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Forbes while it's fresh in your mind. Mr. Karnavas was asking you about Mr. Benabou, and you described his behaviour that he exhibited during the course of those negotiations, when you were trying to, with your colleagues, effect a release of the convoy, that effectively had been taken hostage by the BiH in Mostar. Would you describe his behaviour at the time, was it anti-Muslim?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Did you have the impression from his behaviour at the initial stage, or perhaps all through your familiarity with him, that he was anti-Muslim?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: Yes. That's -- that was my feeling. I think, at that end, that he kind of realised that these people weren't really very religious Muslims, in the sense as you would probably find in the Middle East, and that he was dealing with different people than Israel was dealing with.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Now, just one last question for you. You'll remember that General Praljak asked you, when you were talking about the convoy -- one of the convoys which had come into Mostar, whether you -- you saw him sitting on a vehicle?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Do you remember that question?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And that suggest, to one hearing the question, that you would have known him at the time. Did you know General Praljak at that time?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: No, I didn't. And I'm sure he didn't recognise me either because I was a lot thinner than I am now back then.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: So you hadn't met Mr. Praljak?

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: No, I had not.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions, and I would like to thank you for coming to The Hague and answering questions.

utterances.speaker: LARRY FORBES
utterances.text: You are welcome, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just for the record, Your Honour, as I understand, the word "Mossad" came up on page 190 on line 5, 7, and again on 16. That's "Mossad," M-o-s-s-a-d.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Forbes, I'd like to thank you for having come to testify. We have now completed your testimony, and I would like to wish you a safe journey home to your country. Before we adjourn, I'd like to call upon Mr. Scott to speak about next week's schedule. We will be having an expert next week, Tabeau, Mr. Tabeau, and I believe we will be preparing the whole schedule, the timing, et cetera, and Mr. Tabeau will be continuing the following week. Am I correct? Mrs. Tabeau. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that is correct, and I was just going to say it's Ms. Tabeau. Yes. We expect, Your Honour, given the developments in next week's schedule, she will begin her testimony on Thursday and then will likely be, if I'm not mistaken - I had a look at this just today- if I'm not mistaken, she will be interrupted for a another witness since she's here in The Hague. And it will be concluded after that, but she will be the next week's witness on Thursday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation] Sorry. We need to have the schedule for the next coming weeks, so that we know who is coming when. Repeat: We need to have the schedule for the next few weeks, so that we know who is coming when.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I will work on that, Your Honour. I thought it had gone out; but if it hadn't, it is something that we will address very quickly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I'd like to thank everyone, and we shall resume next week, next Thursday. Between now and then, we will all work very hard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
